transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-18
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Sameer Patel (Redwood SE), Rajiv Menon (CISO - Avalon), Maya Thompson (Platform), Ethan Roe (Infra)

AUTO SUMMARY (auto-generated, may be fuzzy):
Avalon is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private; primary controls: SOC2 attestation, SSO/SAML with SCIM, RBAC requirements for tenant-scoped roles, audit log retention and forwarding to their SIEM, BYOK/KMS/HSM support and key rotation, data residency and retention rules. They want a pilot/bench run to validate latency and log export to Splunk.

TOPICS COVERED:
- SOC2 / ISO posture and documents availability
- SSO (SAML) + SCIM provisioning
- RBAC model, least privilege, admin separation
- Audit logs, retention, streaming to customer SIEM
- Encryption at rest/in transit, BYOK via KMS/HSM
- Data residency, retention, purge requests
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Lena from Redwood Inference, AE on the account. Sameer, our SE, is here. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Rajiv Menon: Doing good, thanks. We have a pretty packed agenda, want to make sure we cover gating items for infosec.
[00:13] Lena Ortiz: Totally. High level first — are you leaning hosted or private today? Curious on constraints.
[00:18] Maya Thompson: We're exploring all three, but the top line is we need SOC2 or equivalent, SSO integration for our internal apps, and the ability to route logs to our Splunk cluster. Also, data can't leave EU for some datasets.
[00:30] Sameer Patel: Makes sense. For SOC2 we can share our Type II attestation, and for ISO 27001 we have a gap plan in process, I can dig in to status. For logs — do you want streaming syslog or an S3 export?
[00:41] Ethan Roe: Prefer streaming or direct ingestion to Splunk HEC. S3 exports are ok but want near real-time for audit trails.
[00:50] Rajiv Menon: Also bring-your-own-key is important for us; we need KMS integration and ideally HSM-backed keys.
[00:57] Lena Ortiz: Great — quick notes: Hosted supports BYOK with cloud KMS integrations today, Dedicated and Private give you more control and can integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM on-prem. There are subtle differences in key rotation policies across modes.
[01:12] Speaker 1: (mumble) KV cash caching — we do prefix caching, sorry that's internal jargon.
[01:18] Sameer Patel: Sorry yes, KV cache, sometimes the transcript says 'KV cash' — we use KV cache for prefix caching to reduce tokens and cost.
[01:25] Maya Thompson: On RBAC, we need to map to our existing roles - developer, infra-admin, security-auditor. Security auditors must have read-only, immutable logs access. Can Redwood map into our SAML groups?
[01:38] Sameer Patel: Yes, we support SAML SSO with group mapping. SCIM provisioning can automatically sync groups for RBAC. We also support role claims so you can map your AD groups to Redwood roles.
[01:49] Rajiv Menon: Any caveats for private cloud or air-gapped? We sometimes need on-prem pockets for PHI workloads.
[01:57] Lena Ortiz: Private deployments (VPC or on-prem package) can be fully air-gapped, but that changes patching cadence and requires a deployment window. We'll surface the maintenance and patch SLAs in the playbook.
[02:10] Ethan Roe: What about audit logs — retention, immutability, and ability to stream? How long do logs sit on Redwood side by default?
[02:18] Sameer Patel: Default retention for our hosted offering is 90 days for application-level logs, but we can extend retention for enterprise accounts and Dedicated/Private can be configured to keep logs in customer-managed storage; we also support streaming via syslog or Kafka, and Splunk HEC like you asked.
[02:32] Maya Thompson: Is there an option to have logs write directly to our S3 with server-side encryption using our KMS key?
[02:39] Sameer Patel: Yes — Dedicated and Private can ship logs to a customer S3 bucket and apply SSE-KMS with your key. For hosted, we can support cross-account S3 or HEC ingestion depending on the integration.
[02:51] Rajiv Menon: About encryption at rest — is hosted encrypted with provider KMS by default and can we bring our own?
[02:58] Lena Ortiz: Hosted encrypts at rest by default with provider-managed keys. BYOK is supported; we also have a roadmap for customer-managed HSMs for high-assurance keys. For Dedicated/Private we anchor to customer KMS.
[03:12] Rajiv Menon: Are keys ever exported or available to Redwood engineers? We need strict separation.
[03:18] Sameer Patel: No, customer keys are not exportable; for BYOK we only have wrapped keys and access is strictly controlled. We can provide the architecture diagram for key usage and rotate recommendations.
[03:28] Ethan Roe: Regulatory question — SOC2 type II OK, but do you have ISO 27001 certification?
[03:34] Lena Ortiz: We are SOC2 Type II attested and ISO 27001 is in progress - current status is documented in the attachments we'll share. I'll send the attestation and a short one-pager on ISO progress.
[03:45] Maya Thompson: Cool. Also need evidence around penetration testing cadence and third-party vulnerability scans.
[03:51] Sameer Patel: We do annual pen tests and quarterly vuln scans; reports can be shared under NDA. We also maintain a public security page with summary controls.
[04:02] Rajiv Menon: How granular is RBAC? Can we limit per-model permissions or data access per team? For us dev teams shouldn't access prod inference logs.
[04:12] Sameer Patel: Yes, role scopes can be per-project and per-model. You can create role bindings that restrict API keys and routes, and we integrate with SSO groups for enforcement. For extra separation we recommend Dedicated or Private to isolate networks and keys.
[04:27] Lena Ortiz: We also have token-level audit fields so you can see which API key and which user invoked an endpoint, and those fields are surfaced to logs.
[04:35] Maya Thompson: Good — SSO flow: do you support SAML 2.0 and SCIM v2?
[04:40] Sameer Patel: SAML 2.0 yes, SCIM v2 yes. Provisioning support includes group push and deprovisioning for account lifecycle.
[04:50] Rajiv Menon: Data residency — we have EU-only requirement for customer PII. How strict is region pinning?
[04:56] Lena Ortiz: Region pinning is supported. For Hosted we have EU regions and you can pin workloads and storage to those regions. Dedicated and Private give you full control over which region or on-prem datacenter is used. We'll show latency tradeoffs in the benchmark.
[05:10] Ethan Roe: On retention and deletion, do you support on-demand purge requests and documented data disposal processes? We may need to satisfy DSARs.
[05:19] Sameer Patel: Yes, we support object-level deletion and can run account-level scrubs on request. There's an audit trail for deletion requests. For DSARs we can coordinate with your legal team; Private gives you the easiest path for full control.
[05:30] Speaker 2: (overlap) Sorry, quick interruption.
[05:33] Lena Ortiz: No problem — continuing — any blockers on procurement/legal side we should know now?
[05:38] Rajiv Menon: Our procurement asks for indemnity language and data processing addendum, plus vendor security questionnaire. We'll send the questionnaire.
[05:46] Lena Ortiz: We'll route that to our legal and security teams; we usually redline the DPA and provide a vendor pack.
[05:51] Maya Thompson: For pilot scope — we'd like to test a model for customer support summarization. Latency SLA target is p95 under 400ms for short prompts. Can Dedicated meet that?
[06:02] Sameer Patel: Dedicated pools are designed for predictable p95s; with right batching and routing you can hit sub-400ms for small seq lengths. We'll need to run your sample prompts and traffic shape. We'll propose a bench with warmed KV cache to simulate production.
[06:17] Rajiv Menon: Are there automated fallbacks if a model variant becomes unavailable? We can't have a cascading outage.
[06:23] Sameer Patel: Smart routing and model fallback can automatically route to a compatible variant; you can set policy to fail open or fail closed. We'll include default fallback policies in the playbook.
[06:35] Maya Thompson: Regarding network security for Private: can you support private link style connectivity or do you require VPN?
[06:42] Lena Ortiz: We support VPC peering, PrivateLink, and VPN. For on-prem we can do direct connect style setups; we'll include network diagrams for each option.
[06:51] Ethan Roe: How do you handle secrets rotation for API keys — we need short-lived tokens and centralized secret rotation.
[06:58] Sameer Patel: We issue API keys and support short-lived credentials via our token service. For deeper integrations, you can use workload identity or mTLS in Private. We also support automated key rotation policies.
[07:10] Rajiv Menon: Audit log immutability — can we have WORM or append-only storage?
[07:15] Sameer Patel: Append-only audit streams can be configured; in Dedicated/Private you can point to an append-only bucket with object lock for WORM semantics. For hosted we have tamper-evident logs and can export to your immutable store.
[07:29] Maya Thompson: Any multi-tenant leakage risks — e.g., cache poisoning across customers?
[07:36] Sameer Patel: We partition KV caches by tenant and have guard rails; we also scrub sensitive prompt text in cache by default unless you opt-in to persistence. We'll share cache partitioning docs.
[07:48] Speaker 1: (faint) question about cost of log retention.
[07:51] Lena Ortiz: Retention extension has cost implications; Redwood Optimize offers reuse/caching suggestions to lower token counts and log volumes. We'll include an estimate in the cost appendix.
[07:59] Rajiv Menon: For compliance evidence, can you provide SOC2 control mappings to our internal control framework?
[08:06] Sameer Patel: Yes, we'll provide a control matrix mapping SOC2 controls to technical controls and evidence artifacts. That's a standard deliverable for enterprise prospects.
[08:16] Maya Thompson: Will you let us run a small smoke bench on hosted first before committing to Dedicated? Our security team prefers to validate log forwarding and SSO before spinning up dedicated capacity.
[08:25] Lena Ortiz: Absolutely — we can do a hosted pilot with strict region pinning and BYOK to validate integrations, then move to Dedicated in the pilot's second phase.
[08:33] Ethan Roe: Time horizons — onboarding timeline for Dedicated? We're aiming for Q2 production if possible.
[08:39] Lena Ortiz: Typical Dedicated lead time is 4-8 weeks including network setup and keys, but it depends on approvals and procurement. If you start pilot this week we can align for Q2.
[08:49] Rajiv Menon: What about breach notification processes and SLA credits?
[08:54] Sameer Patel: We have incident response playbooks, and breach notifications follow contractual timelines in the DPA. SLA credits are in our enterprise contract; we'll surface standard SLA terms.
[09:03] Maya Thompson: One more — do you have SOC2 evidence for pen-testing and access control reviews?
[09:09] Sameer Patel: We can provide redacted pen test summaries under NDA. Access control reviews are part of annual audits.
[09:16] Lena Ortiz: Ok quick recap, we'll: share SOC2 Type II, ISO status, pen-test summary under NDA, private deployment playbook + network diagrams, and a benchmark plan. Any other must-haves?
[09:27] Rajiv Menon: Also the vendor risk questionnaire — we'll send that today.
[09:30] Lena Ortiz: Great. Next steps laid out in the action items. Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with attachments and a proposed date for the benchmark run.

AUTO ACTION ITEMS (end of transcript):
- Lena Ortiz to send SOC2 & ISO status doc (due 2026-02-20)
- Sameer Patel to prepare benchmark checklist and test script (due 2026-02-22)
